DILG BAGONG PIUP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph No S. CAROL AMURAO Municipality of Calintaan Occidental Mindoro Dear Ms. Amurao: This has reference to your email dated January 28, 2025, forwarding to this Department a copy of the Municipal Ordinance No. 2025-01 entitled, "An Ordinance Amending Municipal Zoning Ordinance No. 2 series of 2016 under Article VII Performance Standards Section 21.1 Miscellaneous Regulations, and other Site Development Criteria in Particular to the Minimum Distance of 1,000 Meters to the Nearest Settlement and/or Residential Areas". Your email raised concerns about procedural irregularities in the rezoning ordinance, noting that the Department of Human Settlement and Urban Development (DHSUD) — Environmental, Land Use and Urban Planning and Development Bureau (ELUPDB) has identified issues in the rezoning process. Additionally, in a signature campaign, over five hundred (500) residents within a 1000-meter radius of the proposed construction site for the 25-tonner rice plant oppose the establishment of the rice processing plant in Barangay Poblacion, Calintaan, Occidental Mindoro. We invite your attention to Section 56 (c) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) which reads: "Section 56. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. xxx xxx xxx (c) If the sangguniang panlalawigan finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power conferred upon the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concemed, it shall declare such ordinance or resolution invalid in whole or in part. The sangguniang panlalawigan shall enter its action in the minutes and shall advise the corresponding city or municipal authorities of the action it has taken. " Given that the Municipal Ordinance in question is currently with Sangguniang Panlalawigan and/or the DSHUDI for approval and authentication, the Department, shall refrain from expressing its position on the issue in order to avoid any potential infringement upon their reviewing authority Section 5 of the Municipal Ordinance 2025-01 reads: Section 5 Effectivity — this Amendment Ordinance shall take effect immediately only after approval and authentication by DHSUD or Sangguniang Panlalawigan. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

In the event, however, that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan or DHSUD acted favorably on the Ordinance, the next remedy would be to assail the validity or invalidity of the subject Municipal Ordinance with the court of competent jurisdiction. Let it be stressed that when a Municipal Ordinance is already passed in accordance with the procedural requirements set by the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), they already enjoy the presumption of validity, unless declared otherwise by our courts upon proper judicial action. Thus, if you are convinced that the subject Municipal Ordinance suffers from legal infirmity, we advise you to file a special civil action for declaratory relief pursuant to Section I, Rule 63 of the Revised Rules of Court, which, in part, provides and we quote: "Section l. Who may file petition — Any person interested under a deed, will, contract or other written instrument, whose rights are affected by a statute, executive order or regulation, ordinance, or any govemmental regulation may, before breach or violation thereof, bring an action in the appropriate Regional Trial Court to determine any question of construction or validity arising, and for a declaration of his rights or duties, thereunder." xxx This opinion is based solély on the facts and representations narrated from the letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: A . ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNLLLS-LLRALD/mag Page 2 of 2
